CP16 (blind test): telemetry recovered from orbital physics

Every field below was found without a decoder: candidate byte readings were tested against sunlight, thermal lag, orbital phase, wall-clock time and the IGRF magnetic field computed from the TLE. Names, units and scales are Claude's reading of that evidence, with the satellite name withheld.

Frame type raw:len239

970 frames, 111 passes, 239-byte payload

A 239-byte housekeeping beacon with a wall-clock timer near offset 156, several rolling counters, and a block of sun-dependent power fields at offsets 45-84. The block holds battery or thermal-like bytes, solar-input channels, and a few weak sun-correlated sensors. Many fields are heavily quantized, so the engine's guesses are only moderately reliable.

Health. Several counters show frequent resets: 21 on offsets 141 and 146, plus 13 and 15 on 89 and 97. These are probably rolling counters rather than reboots. The 156 clock has no resets, which argues against recent reboots. The battery-like fields (45-47) rise in sun and fall in shadow with stable ranges, but their daily lows and highs are drifting. That may indicate seasonal variation or early ageing, and there is not enough evidence to say which.
